And the kingdom of the Mongols arose and was renowned in these outer lands,
just as also in those inner lands.
And those Tatars, on their return from Baghdad,
came and encamped against the fortress of Erbil.
And when the son of Salaya wanted and desired to surrender it to them,
many Kurds who were rebelling there turned hostile against him,
and he fled from them to the Tatars.
Then Badr al-Din Lu'lu' came,
and he bought the fortress and all that was in it from the Tatars for seventy thousand dinars.
And the Tatars departed,
and Badr al-Din took possession of the fortress of Erbil,
and he placed guards in it.
And after a little while,
a certain Kurdish emir named Sharaf al-Din Jalali
brought an imperial decree,
and took the fortress from Badr al-Din,
and expelled the guards that he had in it.
And when this Jalali went with the forces of the Tatars against the rebellious Kurds (the rebellious Kurd) of Julamerg,
Badr al-Din sent some Kurds against him,
and they killed him while he was asleep in his tent.
And a Christian man
named Mukhtas,
the brother of Safi Sulayman the great physician,
was appointed to rule over Erbil.
And after his death,
there arose in his place his son Taj al-Din Isa,
a good and faithful man.
And at that time there was a bitter famine and pestilence in all the land of Sinjar, Assyria, Mesopotamia, Syria, and the land of the Romans;
for in Damascus one pomegranate was sold for a sick man for twelve nasiriyahs.
Now when the caliph al-Musta'sim was killed,
the King of Kings appointed over Baghdad a man whose name was Ali Bahadur.
And at that time of destruction, the Tagritan Christians sent to the Catholicos
and requested a prefect (shihna) for themselves to protect them;
and there was sent to them one who guarded them carefully.
